review.assessment: This change introduces `billing/pricing.py` to encapsulate line-item arithmetic and invoice total computation, moving pricing logic out of the main runner. While it cleanly separates concerns, the summation strategy in `total_of` leaves per-line amounts as unrounded floats until a single final quantization step. Because the receipt prints each line rounded to two decimal places, this delayed rounding allows floating-point drift between what is displayed per-line and what is computed for the invoice total.

findings.actual: The sum of printed per-line amounts differs by ±£0.01 from the invoice TOTAL line (e.g., £4888.00 vs £4887.99).
findings.at: Each line is quantized individually before accumulation in `total_of`, and intermediate float calculations are explicitly documented as floats, so rounding drift across multiple lines will inevitably cause the final quantized total to diverge from the sum of printed per-line amounts.
findings.defect: `billing/pricing.py`: `total_of` accumulates raw float `line.total` values and applies `money.quantize` only once at the end. Because the receipt prints each line rounded to two decimal places, summing those printed values will frequently differ by ±£0.01 from the final quantized total due to rounding drift across multiple lines.
findings.expected: The invoice TOTAL line exactly matches the arithmetic sum of its printed per-line amounts.
